Roadmap & Next Steps

What has shipped, and what is queued.

As we validate the feasibility of this architecture, our next milestones include:

  • [x] External MCP client connector: Pluggable connectors package with an HTTP MCP ingest client, CLI adapter, and in-memory tests.
  • [x] Conversational rich surfaces: the studio agent composes validated cards inline from a closed, client-owned catalog instead of describing them in prose.
  • [x] Map ingested evidence onto ODI artifacts: Turn connector records into jobs, outcomes, or evidence without mixing connector plumbing into the ODI store.
  • [x] First-run wizard: A skippable, resumable four-step tour with inline connection repair, ending in the chosen surface or a handoff to the context conversation — isolated in apps/studio/src/onboarding/ behind the firstRunWizard flag.
  • [x] Additional connector kinds: REST/webhooks and similar integrations implementing the same Connector protocol.
  • [x] ODI Schema Definition: Define standardized Pydantic models for Jobs, Steps, and Outcomes.
  • [x] CLI Dataset Commands: Extend apps/cli so the ODI dataset can be created, queried, and scored from the terminal, in addition to the current MCP path.
  • [x] Context Tooling: Replace the dummy greet tool with capabilities like get_job_map(job_id), get_outcomes(job_id), get_step(step_id), get_outcome(outcome_id), or evaluate_outcome(statement).
  • [x] Data Persistence Layer: Connect the FastMCP server to a lightweight SQLite repository containing actual user research data.
  • [x] Agentic Integration: Hook the CLI chat up to an LLM (via the openai package) so the LLM can discover the ODI tools and intelligently request customer insights when ideating features.

Source of truth: docs/roadmap.md — view on GitHub
